摆好棋盘：白方在下，右下角是白格: Set up the board: White at the bottom, light square at the bottom right
棋盘是 8×8 的方格。开始前记住三句话：白棋在下、黑棋在上；右下角是白格；白方: The board has 8×8 squares. Before you start, remember three things: White at the bottom and Black at the top; the bottom-right square is light; White moves first.
白方左下角 a1 是黑格；从白方这头看，左手边一列永远是黑格。: From White's side, a1 in the bottom-left corner is a dark square; the leftmost file is always dark.
白后在白格，黑后在黑格 ——「后爱自己的颜色」，王放在后旁边。: The white queen goes on a light square and the black queen on a dark square — "the queen takes the square of her own color." Place the king beside the queen.
底线从角到中间：车、马、象、后、王；兵排在第二排和第七排。: Along the back rank from each corner toward the center: rook, knight, bishop, queen, king. The pawns go on the second and seventh ranks.
把 a–h 换成 1–8：两个单数或两个双数是黑格，一单一双是白格；a1（11）: Replace a–h with 1–8: two odd numbers or two even numbers mean a dark square; one odd and one even mean a light square. Thus a1 (11) is dark, b1 (21) is light, and a2 (12) is light.
底线怎么摆: How to set up the back rank
两边最外角是车，往里依次是马、象。: The rooks go in the corners. Moving inward, place the knights and then the bishops.
中间两个格子：白后在白格、黑后在黑格 ——「后爱自己的颜色」，王放在后旁边。: The two middle squares: the white queen goes on a light square and the black queen on a dark square — "the queen takes the square of her own color." Place the king beside the queen.
第二排（黑方是第七排）八个格子全是兵。: All eight squares of the second rank are filled with pawns; for Black, this is the seventh rank.
横线用 a 到 h，竖线用 1 到 8；白方左下角是 a1。: Files are labeled a to h, and ranks 1 to 8. From White's side, the bottom-left square is a1.
棋谱里的 e4，就是 e 线第 4 横排那一格。: In chess notation, e4 means the square on the e-file and the fourth rank.
把字母也换成数字：a=1、b=2……h=8。两个数字同为单数或同为双数，格子是黑: Turn the letters into numbers too: a=1, b=2, …, h=8. If both numbers are odd or both are even, the square is dark; if one is odd and the other even, it is light.
例如 a1 是 11，黑格；b1 是 21、a2 是 12，都是白格。: For example, a1 is 11, a dark square; b1 is 21 and a2 is 12, both light squares.
棋子怎么走：走法决定它控制的范围: How the pieces move: movement determines the squares they control
先记住一个核心：棋子能合法走到哪里，就能控制、威胁到哪里（兵是例外，兵攻击的是斜: Start with one key idea: a piece generally controls or threatens the squares it can legally move to. Pawns are the exception because they attack diagonally forward. A piece is valuable not because of its name, but because it can cover important squares. When its position changes, so does its coverage.
先看范围，再看子力: Look at coverage first, then material
车走直线，控制十字；象走斜线，控制 X；马走日字，还能跳过阻挡。: Rooks move in straight lines and control a cross; bishops move diagonally and control an X; knights move in an L shape and can jump over blockers.
王走小米字，后走大米字；兵往前走，斜前方攻击。: The king moves one square in any direction; the queen moves any distance along ranks, files, or diagonals. Pawns move forward but attack diagonally forward.
同样的棋子换个位置，覆盖的格子数可能不同；这就是位置价值。: The same piece may cover a different number of squares in a different position. This is the value of position.
车横着走、竖着走，不能越子；它控制的是从当前位置伸出去的一个十字。: A rook moves horizontally or vertically and cannot jump over pieces. It controls a cross extending from its current square.
在空棋盘中央，车控制 14 格；贴边或困在角落时会变少。: On an empty board, a rook in the center controls 14 squares. It controls fewer on the edge or when trapped in a corner.
车不能一步到斜角，但在空棋盘上多走几步，它能到达任何格子。: A rook cannot reach a diagonally adjacent square in one move, but on an empty board it can reach any square in several moves.
象沿斜线走，不能越子；它控制的是从当前位置伸出去的 X 射线。: A bishop moves along diagonals and cannot jump over pieces. It controls X-shaped lines extending from its current square.
象在不同位置覆盖的格数不同：d4 的象控制 13 格，a1 的象只有 7 格。: A bishop covers different numbers of squares depending on its position: a bishop on d4 controls 13 squares, while one on a1 controls only 7.
象永远只走一种颜色，所以最多覆盖棋盘上一半的格子。: A bishop always stays on one color, so it can cover at most half of the board's squares.
马走「日」字：先直一格再横一格，或者反过来；它是唯一能跳过其他棋子的子。: A knight moves in an L shape: one square straight and then one square sideways, or the reverse. It is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.
和中国象棋的马不同，国际象棋没有「拐子马」规则，旁边有子也能跳。: Unlike the horse in Chinese chess, a knight in international chess has no "blocked horse's leg" rule. It can jump even when pieces are beside it.
马在棋盘中央控制 8 格，在角落只有 2 格；多走几步，马能到达任何格子。: A knight in the center controls 8 squares, but only 2 in a corner. In several moves, it can reach any square.
王：小米字，残局要参战: King: one square in any direction; active in the endgame
王周围八格都能走，但每次只能走一格，所以是「小米字」。: The king can move to any of the eight surrounding squares, but only one square at a time.
王不能走进对方控制的格子；开局要保护它，残局却要尽早让它加入战斗。: The king cannot move into a square controlled by the opponent. Protect it in the opening, but bring it into the fight early in the endgame.
在残局里，活跃的王能护住兵、封住对方王，战斗力不亚于一个车。: In the endgame, an active king can protect pawns and block the opposing king, making it worth nearly as much as a rook.
后把车和象的走法合在一起：横、竖、斜都能走，但不能越子。: The queen combines the rook's and bishop's moves: it can move horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, but it cannot jump over pieces.
它在中央 d4 能控制 27 格，是所有棋子中覆盖率最高的。: On d4 in the center, it controls 27 squares, more than any other piece.
后也不是一步到任何格子；它的威胁来自横、竖、斜三条线。: The queen also cannot reach every square in one move. Its threats come from ranks, files, and diagonals.
兵只向前走，不能后退；从原位出发的第一步可以走一格或两格。: Pawns move forward and never backward. On their first move from the starting square, they may move one or two squares.
兵攻击的是左前方和右前方，不是正前方；只有吃子时，兵才会斜着换到另一列。: Pawns attack one square diagonally forward to the left or right, not straight ahead. A pawn changes files diagonally only when it captures.
兵走到对方底线就能升变，可以选择后、车、象或马，不能选王和兵。: When a pawn reaches the opponent's back rank, it must promote to a queen, rook, bishop, or knight. It cannot become a king or remain a pawn.
吃过路兵：对方兵刚走两格，从你兵的斜前方经过；你必须在下一步立刻斜吃，过后就失去: En passant: when an opposing pawn advances two squares and passes through the square diagonally in front of your pawn, you may capture it diagonally on the very next move. If you wait, the chance is gone.
先看控制范围：在空棋盘上数一数它能覆盖多少格，可以粗略比较活动能力；位置变了，价: First look at coverage: on an empty board, count how many squares a piece can reach to compare its activity roughly. When its position changes, its value changes too.
常用的约定分是兵 1、马 3、象 3、车 5、后 9。这是换算子力的尺子，不是绝: The common point values are pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, and queen 9. These are a rough way to compare material, not absolute prices.
王在普通对局里“无价”：它不能被吃掉，但被将死就输棋；到了残局，活跃的王能护兵、: The king is "priceless" in a normal game: it cannot be captured, but checkmate loses the game. In the endgame, however, an active king can protect pawns and block squares, often working almost like a rook.
后和双车：后约 9 分，双车约 10 分，但没有固定答案。双车配合好、控制开放线: Queen versus two rooks: a queen is worth about 9 points and two rooks about 10, but there is no fixed answer. Two rooks can be stronger when they coordinate well and control open files, while a queen often creates threats more easily.
两个象并不完全相同：一个走白格，一个走黑格，单独看都约 3 分，合在一起却能覆盖: The two bishops are not identical: one travels on light squares and the other on dark squares. Each is worth about 3 points alone, but together they can cover the whole board. This is the "bishop pair" advantage.
双象、双马、一马一象都可能约 6 分。开放局面偏爱双象，封闭局面里马更容易找到前: Two bishops, two knights, or a bishop and a knight may each be worth about 6 points. Open positions favor the bishop pair; in closed positions, knights more easily find strong outposts. Position and coordination ultimately determine value.
马和象同价但不同能：开放斜线适合象，封闭中心和边缘前哨适合马。不要只背分数，要看: Knights and bishops have the same nominal value but different strengths: bishops suit open diagonals, while knights suit closed centers and edge outposts. Do not just memorize points; look at what the piece can do now.
兵形、王的安全、子的活跃度、战术机会和残局阶段都会改变价值；同一枚后在危险位置可: Pawn structure, king safety, piece activity, tactical chances, and the endgame stage all affect value. A queen in a dangerous position can even be worth less than a safe pawn.
想一想：价值为什么会变: Think about it: why does value change?
为什么王不能标成 9 分或 10 分，却能在残局里发挥车的作用？: Why can't the king be given a value of 9 or 10 points, even though it can play the role of a rook in the endgame?
如果开放线上有两辆联动车，对方只有一后，你会只按 9 分和 10 分判断吗？: If you have two coordinated rooks on an open file and your opponent has only a queen, would you judge the position only by 9 points versus 10?
双象一定比双马好吗？如果棋盘塞满兵，答案会变吗？: Are two bishops always better than two knights? Would the answer change if the board were crowded with pawns?
一马一象和双象都是 6 分，为什么教练仍会说“双象更好”？: A bishop and a knight and two bishops are both worth 6 points, so why might a coach still say "two bishops are better"?
特殊规则：将军、将杀、逼和与和棋: Special rules: check, checkmate, stalemate, and draws
会走子以后，还要知道什么时候被将军、什么时候必须应将，以及一盘棋为什么会和。: Once you know how the pieces move, you also need to know when you are in check, when you must respond to it, and why a game can end in a draw.
王正受到攻击叫「将军」。被将军时不能按原计划走棋，必须先解除这次攻击。: When the king is under attack, it is called "check." You cannot continue with your original plan; you must first get out of check.
应将有三种基本办法：把王走到安全格、吃掉攻击的王子、用棋子挡住攻击线。: There are three basic ways to respond to check: move the king to safety, capture the attacking piece, or block the attack with another piece.
如果同时被两路攻击，叫「双将」；通常只能移动王，因为只吃一个子或挡一条线不够。: When two pieces attack the king at once, it is called "double check." Usually the king must move, because capturing one piece or blocking one line is not enough.
不能把王走进另一个受攻击的格子，也不能靠「吃掉对方的王」解将 —— 国际象棋以将: You cannot move your king into another attacked square, and you cannot get out of check by "capturing the opponent's king." Chess ends with checkmate; the king is never actually captured.
王被将军，又没有任何合法办法解将，就是「将死」，被将死的一方输棋。: When the king is in check and there is no legal way to escape, it is "checkmate," and the checkmated side loses.
判断将死要同时看两件事：王正在被攻击，而且所有应将办法都无效。: To decide whether it is checkmate, check two things: the king is under attack, and every possible response to check fails.
只把王将住还不够；如果对方能吃子、挡线或移王脱险，就还没有将死。: Giving check is not enough. If the opponent can capture a piece, block a line, or move the king to safety, it is not checkmate.
「逼和」是轮到你走，却没有合法走法，但王并没有被将军 —— 判和棋。: "Stalemate" means it is your turn, you have no legal move, and your king is not in check. The game is a draw.
将杀是王被攻击且无法解将；逼和是王没被攻击却无路可走，两者结果相反。: In checkmate, the king is attacked and cannot escape. In stalemate, the king is not attacked but has no legal move. The results are opposite.
领先的一方要避免把对方困成逼和，尤其只剩后或车时，要给对方的王留出活动空间。: The side ahead must avoid stalemating the opponent, especially with only a queen or rook. Leave the opposing king some room to move.
和棋让无法取胜的一方仍有防守目标，也让棋局不必靠无限走子硬分胜负。: A draw gives the side that cannot win a defensive goal and prevents a game from dragging on forever just to force a result.
三次重复局面：同一局面出现三次，可以按规则判和；五十回合规则：双方连续五十回合没: Threefold repetition: the same position occurs three times, and a draw may be claimed under the rules. Fifty-move rule: if neither side has made a capture or moved a pawn for fifty consecutive moves, a draw may also be claimed.
双方子力不足以将死时，例如王对王，直接判和；双方同意和棋也是常见结束方式。: When neither side has enough material to force checkmate, such as king versus king, the game is drawn immediately. Agreement between the players is also a common way to end a game.
这些规则不是削弱胜负，而是防止无意义地重复局面、把已经结束的棋一直拖下去。: These rules do not weaken competition. They prevent pointless repetition and keep an already decided game from dragging on.
王和要用的那辆车都没动过，中间也没有别的棋子。: Neither the king nor the rook being used has moved, and there are no pieces between them.
王不能正在被将军；经过的格子和落下的格子也不能被攻击。: The king cannot be in check, and the squares it crosses and lands on cannot be attacked.
走法是王向车走两格，车越过王落到王旁边。: The king moves two squares toward the rook, and the rook jumps over the king to land beside it.
对方兵从原位一步冲两格，正好从你兵的斜前方经过时，你可以把它当作只走了一格，立刻: When an opposing pawn advances two squares from its starting square and passes directly through the square diagonally in front of your pawn, you may capture it diagonally as if it had moved only one square.
白兵在第五横排、黑兵在第四横排时最常遇到：例如白兵 e5、黑兵 d7 刚走到 d: This happens most often with a white pawn on the fifth rank or a black pawn on the fourth rank. For example, if White has a pawn on e5 and Black's pawn has just moved from d7 to d5, White can play e5d6 and capture it en passant.
这个机会只在紧接着的下一步有效；你没有立刻吃，后面就不能再补。: This chance lasts only for the very next move. If you do not take it immediately, you cannot do so later.
兵走到对方底线，必须变成后、车、象或马中的一种，不能变成王或兵。: When a pawn reaches the opponent's back rank, it must become a queen, rook, bishop, or knight. It cannot become a king or a pawn.
通常选后，但有时用车避免逼和，或变成马做出特殊将杀。: A queen is the usual choice, but sometimes a rook avoids stalemate, or a knight creates a special checkmate.
开局三原则：占中心、快出子、早易位: Three opening principles: control the center, develop quickly, castle early
开局不用先背套路。先把中心占住，把轻子放出来，再把王护好；绝大多数普通开局都围绕: You do not need to memorize opening systems first. Control the center, bring out your minor pieces, and keep your king safe. Most ordinary openings follow these three ideas.
开局三原则口诀: Three opening principles: a memory aid
抢占中央：中间四格是交通枢纽，谁站住，谁就有更多支撑点，也能压低对方的调动效率。: Control the center: the four central squares are like transport hubs. Occupying them gives you more support points and makes it harder for your opponent to move pieces efficiently.
快速出子：先出马和象这些轻子；准备短易位时，优先解决王翼的 g1 马和 f1 象: Develop quickly: bring out the knights and bishops first. If you plan to castle kingside, clear the g1 knight and f1 bishop first.
王车易位：王和车都没动过，中间没有子，王也不能走进、穿过或落到被攻击的格子。: Castling: the king and rook must not have moved, the squares between them must be clear, and the king cannot move into, through, or land on an attacked square.
一、抢占中央：为什么四个格子这么重要: 1. Control the center: why these four squares matter
中央四格是 d4、e4、d5、e5。棋子从这里出发，能往更多方向行动，也更容易支: The four central squares are d4, e4, d5, and e5. From here, pieces can move in more directions and support both wings more easily.
占住中心不只是多走几步，而是获得支撑点：马、象和兵可以站在稳固位置，限制对方棋子: Occupying the center is not just about making more moves. It gives you strongpoints where knights, bishops, and pawns can stand securely and restrict the opponent's pieces.
这像足球控制中场、棒球占据垒包、军队争夺交通枢纽；谁掌握中心，谁就更容易调动兵力: It is like controlling midfield in soccer, occupying bases in baseball, or fighting for transport hubs in a military campaign. Whoever controls the center can move forces more easily.
占中心不等于马上把后冲出去。先用兵和小棋子建立空间，再考虑进攻。: Controlling the center does not mean rushing the queen out. First use pawns and minor pieces to build space, then think about attacking.
二、快速出子：先认识轻子和重子: 2. Develop quickly: minor pieces and major pieces
马和象叫轻子，车和后叫重子。开局阶段轻子灵活，通常先让马和象离开底线。: Knights and bishops are minor pieces; rooks and queens are major pieces. Minor pieces are flexible in the opening, so knights and bishops usually leave the back rank first.
出子的重点是“出新子”，不是反复挪同一个子；每走一步，尽量让一个新棋子加入战斗。: Development means bringing out new pieces, not moving the same piece repeatedly. With each move, try to bring another piece into the game.
如果准备短易位，先处理王翼的 g1 马和 f1 象；如果准备长易位，则要处理后翼: For kingside castling, clear the kingside g1 knight and f1 bishop. For queenside castling, clear the queenside b1 knight, c1 bishop, and d1 queen.
一条常见的白方短易位流程是 1.e4、2.Nf3、3.Bc4、4.O-O：第一步: One common White kingside-castling sequence is 1.e4, 2.Nf3, 3.Bc4, 4.O-O: claim the center on move one, develop the minor pieces over the next two moves, and castle on move four.
这只是示意，不是唯一答案；对手走法、战术威胁和开局体系都会改变顺序。: This is only an example, not the only answer. The opponent's moves, tactical threats, and opening system can change the order.
王和参与易位的车都必须没有移动过；王与车之间不能有任何棋子。: Both the king and the rook used for castling must not have moved, and no pieces may stand between them.
王不能正在被将军；王经过的格子和最终落下的格子也不能被攻击。攻击线同样算阻碍。: The king cannot be in check, and the squares it crosses and lands on cannot be attacked. An attacked square along the path also prevents castling.
短易位是王向 h 侧走两格到 g1，车到 f1；长易位是王向 a 侧走两格到 c: In kingside castling, the king moves two squares toward the h-side to g1 and the rook goes to f1. In queenside castling, the king moves two squares toward the a-side to c1 and the rook goes to d1.
短易位通常更快，王躲在王翼兵后比较安全，车也更容易支援中路；但进攻方向可能更集中: Kingside castling is usually faster. The king is often safer behind the kingside pawns, and the rook can support the center more easily, though the attack may become more concentrated on that side.
长易位让王去后翼，车占据 d 线，常给王翼留出推进空间；不过要清开的子更多，后翼: Queenside castling places the king on the queenside and the rook on the d-file, often leaving space for a kingside advance. However, more pieces must be cleared, and the queenside may be more exposed.
长短易位没有绝对好坏，要看兵形、对方棋子、开放线和你的进攻计划。: Neither side of castling is always better. It depends on the pawn structure, the opponent's pieces, open files, and your attacking plan.
想一想：最快几步能完成三原则: Think about it: how few moves does it take to follow all three principles?
如果对手不干扰，白方可以像 1.e4、2.Nf3、3.Bc4、4.O-O 这样在: If the opponent does not interfere, White can follow a sequence like 1.e4, 2.Nf3, 3.Bc4, 4.O-O to control the center, develop pieces, and castle kingside by move four.
长易位通常需要先清开 b1 马、c1 象和 d1 后，顺利时往往要到第五步；为什: Queenside castling usually requires clearing the b1 knight, c1 bishop, and d1 queen first, so it often takes until move five. Why is this extra move needed?
如果对方已经控制 f1 或 g1，你还能短易位吗？如果不能，应该先改计划还是硬走: If the opponent already controls f1 or g1, can you still castle kingside? If not, should you change the plan or force it?
常见战术：先找强制手，再算对手应手: Common tactics: find forcing moves first, then calculate the opponent's replies
战术就是几步之内能占到便宜的手段。真正值得练的不是背答案，而是每次都先找将军、吃: Tactics are short sequences that win material or achieve another advantage. The skill to practice is not memorizing answers, but always looking first for checks, captures, and threats, then calculating the opponent's replies to the end.
一找强制手：将军、吃子、直接威胁，先看这些走法。: 1. Look for forcing moves: checks, captures, and direct threats come first.
二算应手：对手能逃、能挡、能反将军，不要只算自己顺利的那条线。: 2. Calculate replies: the opponent may escape, block, or give check. Do not calculate only the line that goes well for you.
三走到底：把整条解法走完，确认最后真的赢子或将死。: 3. Play to the end: complete the whole solution and confirm that it really wins material or gives checkmate.

国象礼仪：认真对局，也尊重对手: Chess etiquette: play seriously and respect your opponent
礼仪不是客套，而是让双方都能专心思考。真正重要的只有几句话：确认规则、落子负责、: Etiquette is not just politeness; it helps both players concentrate. The essentials are simple: agree on the rules, take responsibility for your moves, do not disturb your opponent, and behave well whether you win or lose.
开局先问好，颜色和时限确认好。: Greet your opponent before the game and confirm the colors and time control.
正式比赛要调整棋子，先说 adjust，再伸手。: In formal games, say "adjust" before reaching over to straighten a piece.
不催、不嘲讽、不用引擎；轮到自己走时再提和。: Do not rush, mock, or use an engine. Offer a draw only when it is your turn.
认输不掀棋盘，赛后说声好棋，再一起复盘。: Do not overturn the board when you resign. After the game, say "good game," then review together.
先向对手问好，确认谁拿白棋、用什么时限，以及是否按正式比赛规则进行。: Greet your opponent and confirm who has White, what time control is being used, and whether formal tournament rules apply.
摆好棋盘和棋子；需要调整位置时，在正式比赛中先说「adjust」，再动手摆正。: Set up the board and pieces correctly. If a piece needs adjusting in a formal game, say "adjust" before moving it.
确认时钟和行棋方向，避免开局后才发现双方理解不同。: Confirm the clock and the direction of play so you do not discover a misunderstanding after the game has started.
正式面对面比赛通常实行「触摸走子」：碰了自己的棋子，就应走出这个子；碰了对方的棋: Formal over-the-board games usually use the touch-move rule: if you touch one of your pieces, you must move it; if you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it, provided the move is legal.
所以调整棋子要先说「adjust」，不要随手把棋子摆来摆去。: That is why you should say "adjust" before repositioning a piece instead of moving pieces casually.
想换一步就提前想好；落子后不要拿回重走，线上对局也应养成同样的思考习惯。: Decide whether you want to change a move before making it. Once you release a piece, do not take it back; build the same careful thinking habits online.
对手思考时保持安静，不催促、不做表情干扰、不频繁离开座位。: Stay quiet while your opponent thinks. Do not rush them, distract them with expressions, or leave your seat repeatedly.
不用手机、引擎或场外帮助；即使只是想看一眼提示，也已经破坏公平。: Do not use a phone, chess engine, or outside help. Even glancing at a hint breaks fair play.
领先时不嚣张，落后时不发脾气；你的目标是走出好棋，不是让对手难受。: Do not gloat when you are ahead or lose your temper when you are behind. Your goal is to play good chess, not to make your opponent uncomfortable.
提和、认输与赛后: Draw offers, resignation, and after the game
提和通常在轮到自己走时进行：先停下时钟、提出和棋，再决定是否落子；对方可以接受或: A draw is usually offered on your turn: stop the clock, offer the draw, and then decide whether to make a move. Your opponent may accept or decline.
局面已经无法挽回时，可以坦然认输，说一句「我认输」，不要故意拖延或把棋盘弄乱。: When the position is beyond saving, resign graciously by saying "I resign." Do not delay on purpose or scatter the pieces.
结束后握手，说声「好棋」或「谢谢」；想复盘就简短、具体，不责怪、不翻旧账。: After the game, shake hands and say "good game" or "thank you." If you review the game, keep it brief and specific; do not blame or reopen old disputes.
聊天简短礼貌，不发送嘲讽、威胁或无关信息。: Keep chat brief and polite. Do not send insults, threats, or unrelated messages.
同样不使用引擎或场外帮助；网络对局也讲究公平和尊重。: The same rule applies online: no engines or outside help. Fair play and respect matter on the internet too.
遇到争议先按平台规则处理，不在聊天窗口里争吵。: Handle disputes according to the platform's rules instead of arguing in the chat window.
国际象棋既是人的思维训练，也是人工智能的经典试验场。它把规则、状态、选择和结果摆: Chess is both mental training for people and a classic testing ground for artificial intelligence. On a finite board, it brings together rules, states, choices, and outcomes, letting us clearly study how to make good decisions.

下棋和写代码都要遵守规则、列出可能、验证结果。: Both chess and coding require following rules, listing possibilities, and verifying results.
AlphaGo 的突破不是只靠算得更快，而是用神经网络、强化学习和自我对弈学会判: AlphaGo's breakthrough was not just faster calculation. It used neural networks, reinforcement learning, and self-play to learn how to judge positions.
搜索树帮我们探索分支；复盘和测试帮我们发现错误。: Search trees help us explore branches; review and testing help us find mistakes.
为什么影视作品里的天才喜欢下棋: Why geniuses in films like chess
棋盘把看不见的思考变成了看得见的动作：落子、停顿、反击，观众很容易看懂。: The board turns invisible thinking into visible actions: making a move, pausing, counterattacking. The audience can easily follow.
国际象棋规则有限、信息透明，又需要计算和布局，很适合表现一个人「能比别人多想几步: Chess has limited rules and open information, yet it requires calculation and planning. It is ideal for showing that someone can think several moves ahead.
所以影视常用下棋象征策略、冷静和智力对决；这是一种常见的叙事手法，不是聪明人的统: Films and television therefore often use chess to symbolize strategy, calm, and intellectual conflict. It is a common storytelling device, not a universal hobby of intelligent people and certainly not proof of intelligence.
为什么科技圈流行下棋: Why chess is popular in tech
下棋要求在规则限制下不断做取舍：先发展还是先进攻，保留子力还是冒险抢速度。: Chess constantly forces trade-offs within the rules: develop first or attack first, preserve material or take a risk for speed.
它能训练模式识别、注意力、风险判断和从失败中复盘，这些能力也能迁移到产品与技术工: It trains pattern recognition, attention, risk judgment, and learning from failure—skills that also transfer to product and technical work.
棋类活动还有社交和竞技的一面，因此受到许多科技从业者欢迎；但它不是硅谷的入场券，: Chess also has social and competitive sides, which is why many technology professionals enjoy it. But it is not a ticket into Silicon Valley or a measure of a person's worth.
为什么 AI 研究盯上了国际象棋: Why AI researchers focused on chess
国际象棋规则明确、状态有限、信息完全公开，电脑可以准确模拟每一步，也容易判断谁赢: Chess has clear rules, a finite set of states, and completely open information. A computer can simulate every move accurately and determine who wins.
它不需要摄像头、机器人或模糊的人类语言，适合先研究搜索、评估和决策这些核心问题。: It requires no cameras, robots, or ambiguous human language, making it well suited to studying core problems such as search, evaluation, and decision-making.
早期 AI 也研究跳棋、谜题和逻辑证明，国际象棋只是最有代表性的试验场之一，并不: Early AI also studied checkers, puzzles, and logical proofs. Chess was one of the most representative testing grounds, not the only starting point.
1997 年，Deep Blue 击败国际象棋世界冠军卡斯帕罗夫。它主要依靠强大: In 1997, Deep Blue defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov. It relied mainly on powerful search, position evaluation, and specialized hardware, proving that a computer could beat top humans at chess.
2016 年，AlphaGo 以 4:1 战胜李世石。围棋的分支远多于国际象棋，: In 2016, AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol 4–1. Go has far more possible branches than chess, so brute force and hand-written rules alone were not enough. AlphaGo combined deep neural networks, reinforcement learning, Monte Carlo tree search, and self-play.
AlphaGo 的关键不只是「算得快」，而是从大量自我对弈中学会判断局面，并搜索: AlphaGo's key was not merely "calculating quickly." It learned to judge positions from extensive self-play and searched the most promising branches.
后来 AlphaZero 又通过自我对弈学习国际象棋、将棋和围棋，说明通用学习方: Later, AlphaZero learned chess, shogi, and Go through self-play, showing that a general learning method can reach a high level in different rule systems.
国际象棋训练哪些思维能力: What thinking skills does chess train?
逻辑与因果：每一步都会改变局面，必须考虑对手回应，不能只看自己想要的剧本。: Logic and cause and effect: every move changes the position. You must consider your opponent's replies, not just the story you want to follow.
规则意识：再漂亮的棋，只要是非法走法就不能成立；算法也必须遵守同样的约束。: Rule awareness: however attractive a move looks, it is invalid if it breaks the rules. Algorithms must obey the same constraints.
计划与调整：开局先有原则，但对手走出新变化时，必须重新评估并改计划。: Planning and adjustment: start the opening with principles, but when the opponent finds a new variation, reassess and change the plan.
复盘与纠错：输棋后找具体原因，把一次失误变成下一次能识别的模式。: Review and correction: after a loss, find the specific cause and turn one mistake into a pattern you can recognize next time.
棋谱为什么像代码: Why chess notation is like code
FEN 像程序里的状态快照：它记录当前局面；PGN 像一串合法操作：它记录怎样从: FEN is like a state snapshot in a program: it records the current position. PGN is like a sequence of legal operations: it records how to move from that state to the next.
开局树像代码里的分支结构：同一个根局面可以走向不同变化，每个选择又会引出新的可能: An opening tree is like a branching structure in code: one root position can lead to different variations, and each choice opens new possibilities.
下棋要检查合法性，写代码要检查语法、类型和测试；下完棋要复盘，程序出错要调试。: In chess you check legality; in coding you check syntax, types, and tests. After a game you review it; when a program fails you debug it.
两者都训练同一件事：在明确规则下，把复杂问题拆成状态、操作、分支和结果。: Both train the same skill: breaking a complex problem into states, operations, branches, and outcomes under explicit rules.
蒙特卡洛树搜索和开局树的相似之处: Similarities between Monte Carlo tree search and an opening tree
两者都从一个根局面出发，把可走的棋看成子节点，再沿着分支不断展开。: Both start from one root position, treat legal moves as child nodes, and expand along branches.
蒙特卡洛树搜索会反复选择、扩展、模拟和回传结果，让有希望的分支得到更多关注。: Monte Carlo tree search repeatedly selects, expands, simulates, and backs up results, giving more attention to promising branches.
开局树则主要记录人类积累的变化和经验，帮助棋手快速找到常见计划与陷阱。: An opening tree mainly records variations and experience accumulated by humans, helping players find common plans and traps quickly.
它们都体现「探索—评估—更新」的思路，但不是同一种算法：现代国际象棋引擎主要用: Both reflect an "explore–evaluate–update" approach, but they are not the same algorithm. Modern chess engines mainly use Alpha-Beta search and neural-network evaluation, while Monte Carlo tree search is better known in Go.
